topic: The Pi Mystery: Counting Collisions to Calculate Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school students or curious science enthusiasts

sections.title: The Setup: The Two-Block Collision Puzzle
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless floor.
Block A moves toward Block B.
Block B bounces off a wall.
Block B strikes Block A again.
We count total collisions until they separate.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Elastic Collisions and Momentum
lecture_lines: Collisions conserve both momentum and energy.
Elastic bounces keep total energy constant.
Velocity vectors change during every impact.
animations: Define momentum equation: p = mv. Label in #FFFFFF.
Show elastic collision: Energy conserved. Label in #FFFF00.
Show momentum conservation: Total momentum stays constant. Label #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Unexpected Pattern: Scaling Mass
lecture_lines: Mass ratios affect the collision count.
Powers of one hundred reveal Pi.
The digits of Pi appear naturally.

The number of bounces equals Pi.
